findings.text: _arming_has_gone() decides the arming has gone from os.getppid() being dead, but follower_registration.py:559-564 records that after an arming session dies its parent names init or a subreaper; under a live subreaper getppid() is alive, _arming_has_gone() returns False and the reader substitution never fires, so the defect §134 describes persists in exactly the state the module's own comment says re-parenting produces. The discriminator should compare the current parent against the recorded owner from follower_owner(), not merely test the parent's liveness.

the blockers line records that the population arm over the files importing reckon/crew_follow_commands.py was never run, a done-when item §134 states as required evidence, and scratch/head-all-three.log records its '# cwd:' as the worktree rather than an all_debug partition job as the done-when specifies.

the tests field is a prose description of three runs rather than the literal command a shell was handed, so promotion cannot fill its gate receipt from this line and refuses it; the commands that actually ran are on the '# cmd:' header lines of the logs named in test_logs.

_stdout_has_reader() answers False for stat.S_ISSOCK and stat.S_ISCHR, so an orphaned follower whose stdout is a socket or a terminal, both readers under §134's deliverable, still ends and frees its registration; the narrowing to pipes is documented in the docstring but is a narrower reading than the plan states.

_pipe_reader_pids, and delivery_mode at :199, already answer whether anything holds a pipe's read end; _stdout_has_reader adds a second mechanism for that one capability rather than extending the owner, defensible only because its POLLERR probe is cheap where the /proc walk is memoised at 211 ms.

the local owner_alive shadows the module-level owner_alive function imported at line 33 and used at line 1025, and the two differ in semantics — the imported one requires a recorded start_time while the local one skips the start check when it is empty — so a later call in this scope would silently receive a bool.

baseline_suite and after_suite omit the required failure_count key, so both arms are shape-incomplete; the counts derive from the named logs as 1 (scratch/base-arm.log) and 0 (scratch/head-all-three.log).

the fragment asserts the ruff result at the head, but the only ruff log (scratch/ruff-check.log) carries no revision header and ends FORMAT_EXIT=1 with the new test unformatted, so no head-revision receipt exists for that done-when item; re-run at ee25b58b3c the test is format-clean and the only findings are SIM103 and SIM115, both present at base.
